manner.en: died of fever after six days

sourceDate.text: 梁王二十二年，孝文帝崩

manner.en: beheaded and displayed in the marketplace

value.action: robbed and murdered travelers at night

units.zh: 梁孝王武者，孝文皇帝子也，而與孝景帝同母。
units.en: King Xiao of Liang, whose given name was Wu, was a son of Emperor Wen, born of the same mother as Emperor Jing.
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Liang, Liu Wu, was a son of Emperor Xiaowen, and shared the same mother as Emperor Xiaojing.

units.zh: 母，竇太后也。
units.en: Their mother was Empress Dowager Dou.
units.literal: Their mother was Empress Dowager Dou.

units.zh: 孝文帝凡四男：長子曰太子，是為孝景帝；
units.en: Emperor Wen had four sons in all. The eldest was appointed Crown Prince and would later become Emperor Jing.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen had four sons altogether: the eldest son was the Crown Prince, who became Emperor Xiaojing;

units.zh: 次子武；
units.en: The second was Wu.
units.literal: the second son was Wu;

units.zh: 次子參；
units.en: The third was Can.
units.literal: the third son was Can;

units.zh: 次子勝。
units.en: And the fourth was Sheng.
units.literal: the fourth son was Sheng.

units.zh: 孝文帝即位二年，以武為代王，以參為太原王，以勝為梁王。
units.en: In the second year after Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Sheng as King of Liang.
units.literal: In the second year after Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Sheng as King of Liang.

units.zh: 二歲，徙代王為淮陽王。
units.en: Two years later, he transferred the King of Dai to serve as King of Huaiyang.
units.literal: Two years later, he transferred the King of Dai to be King of Huaiyang.

units.zh: 以代盡與太原王，號曰代王。
units.en: The territory of Dai was given entirely to the King of Taiyuan, who then assumed the title King of Dai.
units.literal: He gave all of Dai to the King of Taiyuan, who was then titled King of Dai.

units.zh: 參立十七年，孝文後二年卒，謚為孝王。
units.en: Can reigned for seventeen years and died in the second year of Emperor Wen's Later Reign. He was posthumously titled King Xiao.
units.literal: Can reigned seventeen years, died in the second year of Xiaowen's Later Reign, and received the posthumous title King Xiao.

units.zh: 子登嗣立，是為代共王。
units.en: His son Deng succeeded him and became King Gong of Dai.
units.literal: His son Deng succeeded him, becoming King Gong of Dai.

units.zh: 立二十九年，元光二年卒。
units.en: He reigned for twenty-nine years and died in the second year of the Yuanguang era.
units.literal: He reigned twenty-nine years, died in Yuanguang year 2.

units.zh: 子義立，是為代王。
units.en: His son Yi succeeded him and became King of Dai.
units.literal: His son Yi succeeded him, becoming King of Dai.

units.zh: 十九年，漢廣關，以常山為限，而徙代王王清河。
units.en: Nineteen years later, the Han court extended the frontier passes, setting Mount Changshan as the boundary, and transferred the King of Dai to rule over Qinghe.
units.literal: Nineteen years later, Han expanded the passes, using Changshan as the boundary, and transferred the King of Dai to rule Qinghe.

units.zh: 清河王徙以元鼎三年也。
units.en: This transfer to Qinghe took place in the third year of the Yuanding era.
units.literal: The King of Qinghe's transfer was in Yuanding year 3.

units.zh: 初，武為淮陽王十年，而梁王勝卒，謚為梁懷王。
units.en: Earlier, Wu had served as King of Huaiyang for ten years when the King of Liang, Sheng, died and was posthumously titled King Huai of Liang.
units.literal: Initially, Wu served as King of Huaiyang for ten years, while the King of Liang Sheng died, posthumous title King Huai of Liang.

units.zh: 懷王最少子，愛幸異於他子。
units.en: King Huai had been the youngest son and was loved and favored far more than his brothers.
units.literal: King Huai was the youngest son, loved and favored differently from the other sons.

units.zh: 其明年，徙淮陽王武為梁王。
units.en: The following year, the King of Huaiyang, Wu, was transferred to become King of Liang.
units.literal: The next year, he transferred the King of Huaiyang Wu to be King of Liang.

units.zh: 梁王之初王梁，孝文帝之十二年也。
units.en: The King of Liang first received his fief in the twelfth year of Emperor Wen's reign.
units.literal: The King of Liang's first enfeoffment in Liang was in Emperor Xiaowen's twelfth year.

units.zh: 梁王自初王通歷已十一年矣。
units.en: By this time, the King of Liang had already held a royal title for eleven years since his first enfeoffment.
units.literal: The King of Liang, from his initial enfeoffment to now, had experienced eleven years.

units.zh: 梁王十四年，入朝。
units.en: In his fourteenth year, the King of Liang traveled to the capital for a court audience.
units.literal: In the King of Liang's fourteenth year, he entered court.

units.zh: 十七年，十八年，比年入朝，留，其明年，乃之國。
units.en: In his seventeenth and eighteenth years, he attended court in consecutive years and stayed on, returning to his kingdom only the following year.
units.literal: In years seventeen and eighteen, he entered court consecutively, remained, and only the next year returned to his fief.

units.zh: 二十一年，入朝。
units.en: In his twenty-first year, he again attended court.
units.literal: In year twenty-one, he entered court.

units.zh: 二十二年，孝文帝崩。
units.en: In his twenty-second year, Emperor Wen passed away.
units.literal: In year twenty-two, Emperor Xiaowen passed away.

units.zh: 二十四年，入朝。
units.en: In his twenty-fourth year, he attended court.
units.literal: In year twenty-four, he entered court.

units.zh: 二十五年，復入朝。
units.en: In his twenty-fifth year, he attended court once more.
units.literal: In year twenty-five, he entered court again.

units.zh: 是時上未置太子也。
units.en: At that time, the emperor had not yet designated a crown prince.
units.literal: At this time the emperor had not yet established a crown prince.

units.zh: 上與梁王燕飲，嘗從容言曰：「千秋萬歲後傳於王。」
units.en: During a private banquet with the King of Liang, the emperor once remarked casually, "When I am gone, I shall pass the throne to you."
units.literal: The emperor and the King of Liang were feasting together, and the emperor once said casually, "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, I shall pass the throne to you."

units.zh: 王辭謝。
units.en: The king politely declined.
units.literal: The king declined politely.

units.zh: 雖知非至言，然心內喜。
units.en: Though he knew the words were not meant in earnest, he was secretly delighted.
units.literal: Though he knew these were not serious words, in his heart he was inwardly pleased.

units.zh: 太后亦然。
units.en: The Empress Dowager felt the same.
units.literal: The empress dowager was the same.

units.zh: 其春，吳楚齊趙七國反。
units.en: That spring, the seven kingdoms — Wu, Chu, Qi, Zhao, and the rest — rose in rebellion.
units.literal: That spring, Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao—the seven kingdoms—rebelled.

units.zh: 吳楚先擊梁棘壁，殺數萬人。
units.en: Wu and Chu first struck at the fortress of Jibi in Liang, killing tens of thousands.
units.literal: Wu and Chu first attacked Liang's Ji Wall, killing tens of thousands.

units.zh: 梁孝王城守睢陽，而使韓安國、張羽等為大將軍，以距吳楚。
units.en: King Xiao of Liang held fast within the walls of Suiyang, dispatching Han Anguo, Zhang Yu, and others as grand generals to resist Wu and Chu.
units.literal: Prince Xiao of Liang defended the city of Suiyang, and sent Han Anguo, Zhang Yu and others as grand generals to resist Wu and Chu.

units.zh: 吳楚以梁為限，不敢過而西，與太尉亞夫等相距三月。
units.en: Wu and Chu were checked by Liang and dared not press westward, remaining locked in a standoff with Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu and his forces for three months.
units.literal: Wu and Chu used Liang as their limit, dared not cross west, and confronted Grand Commandant Yafu and others for three months.

units.zh: 吳楚破，而梁所破殺虜略與漢中分。
units.en: When Wu and Chu were finally crushed, the enemy forces that Liang had routed, slain, and captured rivaled the tally of the imperial armies.
units.literal: Wu and Chu were defeated, and Liang's captured, killed, and plundered was shared equally with Han.

units.zh: 明年，漢立太子。
units.en: The following year, the Han court formally established a crown prince.
units.literal: The next year, Han established the crown prince.

units.zh: 其後梁最親，有功，又為大國，居天下膏腴地。
units.en: After these events, Liang stood closest to the throne in kinship, had earned great merit, and ranked among the largest kingdoms, its lands encompassing the most fertile territory in the empire.
units.literal: Afterwards Liang was closest, had merit, was also a great kingdom, occupying the fertile lands of the realm.

units.zh: 地北界泰山，西至高陽，四十餘城，皆多大縣。
units.en: Its territory stretched north to Mount Tai and west to Gaoyang, comprising more than forty cities, all of them large and populous counties.
units.literal: Its territory bordered Mount Tai in the north, reached Gaoyang in the west, over forty cities, all with many large counties.

units.zh: 孝王，竇太后少子也，愛之，賞賜不可勝道。
units.en: King Xiao was the youngest son of Empress Dowager Dou, who loved him dearly and showered him with gifts and rewards beyond reckoning.
units.literal: Prince Xiao was Empress Dowager Dou's youngest son, she loved him, rewards and grants beyond counting.

units.zh: 於是孝王筑東苑，方三百餘里。
units.en: King Xiao built the Eastern Park, which stretched more than three hundred li on each side.
units.literal: Thus, Prince Xiao built the Eastern Park, covering over three hundred li square.

units.zh: 廣睢陽城七十里。
units.en: He expanded the walls of Suiyang by seventy li.
units.literal: He expanded Suiyang city seventy li.

units.zh: 大治宮室，為複道，自宮連屬於平臺三十餘里。
units.en: He built grand palaces and constructed covered walkways that ran from the palace to the Terrace, extending more than thirty li without interruption.
units.literal: He greatly constructed palaces, built covered walkways connecting from the palace to the Platform for over thirty li.

units.zh: 得賜天子旌旗，出從千乘萬騎。
units.en: He was granted the imperial banners of the Son of Heaven, and when he went abroad, a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen followed in his train.
units.literal: He received the emperor's banners and flags as grants, went out followed by a thousand chariots and ten thousand cavalry.

units.zh: 東西馳獵，擬於天子。
units.en: He hunted east and west in a splendor rivaling that of the Son of Heaven himself.
units.literal: He galloped hunting east and west, comparable to the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 出言蹕，入言警。
units.en: When he went abroad, heralds cried 'Clear the way!' and when he returned, they called 'Be alert!'
units.literal: When going out he used 'clear the way,' when entering he used 'be alert.'

units.zh: 招延四方豪桀，自山以東游說之士。
units.en: He recruited heroes and men of talent from every quarter, as well as itinerant persuaders from east of the mountains.
units.literal: He recruited and welcomed heroes and outstanding men from the four directions, wandering persuaders from east of the mountains.

units.zh: 莫不畢至，齊人羊勝、公孫詭、鄒陽之屬。
units.en: All of them flocked to his court — men of Qi such as Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang.
units.literal: None failed to arrive completely—men from Qi like Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, Zou Yang and such.

units.zh: 公孫詭多奇邪計，初見王，賜千金，官至中尉，梁號之曰公孫將軍，梁多作兵器弩弓矛數十萬，而府庫金錢且百巨萬，珠玉寶器多於京師。
units.en: Gongsun Gui was a man of many cunning and unorthodox schemes. At his first audience with the king, he was granted a thousand catties of gold, and his rank rose to Commandant of the Capital. In Liang, he was known as General Gongsun. The kingdom manufactured hundreds of thousands of weapons — crossbows, bows, and spears — while its treasury held nearly a hundred million in gold and cash, and its pearls, jade, and precious objects exceeded those of the imperial capital.
units.literal: Gongsun Gui had many strange and crooked schemes, first meeting the king, granted a thousand jin, office reaching Commandant of the Guards, Liang titled him General Gongsun, Liang made many weapons—crossbows, bows, spears—several tens of thousands, while the treasury had gold and cash nearly a hundred million, pearls, jade, and precious objects more than the capital.

units.zh: 二十九年十月，梁孝王入朝。
units.en: In the tenth month of his twenty-ninth year, King Xiao of Liang traveled to court.
units.literal: In year twenty-nine, tenth month, Prince Xiao of Liang entered court.

units.zh: 景帝使使持節乘輿駟馬，迎梁王於關下。
units.en: Emperor Jing dispatched envoys bearing the imperial tally, with a chariot drawn by four horses, to welcome the King of Liang at the pass.
units.literal: Emperor Jing sent envoys holding the tally with imperial chariot and four horses, to welcome the King of Liang at the pass.

units.zh: 既朝，上疏因留，以太后親故。
units.en: After attending court, he submitted a memorial requesting permission to remain in the capital, citing his close bond with the Empress Dowager.
units.literal: Having attended court, he submitted a memorial requesting to remain, because of the empress dowager's close relation.

units.zh: 王入則侍景帝同輦，出則同車游獵，射禽獸上林中。
units.en: At court the king rode in the same carriage as Emperor Jing; abroad they hunted together, shooting birds and beasts in the Shanglin Park.
units.literal: When the king entered he served Emperor Jing in the same chariot, when going out they rode in the same carriage hunting, shooting birds and beasts in Shanglin Park.

units.zh: 梁之侍中、郎、謁者著籍引出入天子殿門，與漢宦官無異。
units.en: Liang's palace attendants, gentlemen, and ushers were registered and allowed to pass freely through the gates of the Son of Heaven's palace, no differently from the Han court officials themselves.
units.literal: Liang's attendants-in-ordinary, gentlemen, and ushers were registered and led in and out of the Son of Heaven's palace gates, no different from Han eunuchs.

units.zh: 十一月，上廢栗太子，竇太后心欲以孝王為後嗣。
units.en: In the eleventh month, the emperor deposed Crown Prince Li. Empress Dowager Dou secretly wished to make King Xiao the heir apparent.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor deposed Crown Prince Li, Empress Dowager Dou's heart wished to make Prince Xiao the successor.

units.zh: 大臣及袁盎等有所關說於景帝，竇太后義格，亦遂不復言以梁王為嗣事由此。
units.en: The great ministers and Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Jing. Empress Dowager Dou, moved by considerations of propriety, relented and from that point on never again raised the matter of making the King of Liang the heir.
units.literal: The ministers and Yuan Ang and others remonstrated with Emperor Jing. Empress Dowager Dou, restrained by considerations of propriety, relented and from that point no longer spoke of making the King of Liang the successor.

units.zh: 以事秘，世莫知。
units.en: Because the affair was kept secret, the world at large knew nothing of it.
units.literal: Because the matter was secret, the world did not know.

units.zh: 乃辭歸國。
units.en: The king then took his leave and returned to his kingdom.
units.literal: So he took leave and returned home.

units.zh: 其夏四月，上立膠東王為太子。
units.en: That summer, in the fourth month, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince.
units.literal: That summer, fourth month, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince.

units.zh: 梁王怨袁盎及議臣，乃與羊勝、公孫詭之屬陰使人刺殺袁盎及他議臣十餘人。
units.en: The King of Liang harbored a deep grudge against Yuan Ang and the other ministers who had spoken against him. Together with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their associates, he secretly dispatched assassins who murdered Yuan Ang and more than ten of the other ministers who had advised against the succession.
units.literal: The King of Liang resented Yuan Ang and the discussing ministers, so secretly sent men with Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and others to assassinate Yuan Ang and more than ten other discussing ministers.

units.zh: 逐其賊，未得也。
units.en: The authorities pursued the assassins but failed to apprehend them.
units.literal: They pursued the assassins, did not catch them.

units.zh: 於是天子意梁王，逐賊，果梁使之。
units.en: The Son of Heaven suspected the King of Liang, and when the assassins were tracked down, it was indeed confirmed that Liang had sent them.
units.literal: Thus, the Son of Heaven suspected the King of Liang, pursuing the assassins—indeed it was Liang who sent them.

units.zh: 乃遣使冠蓋相望於道，覆按梁，捕公孫詭、羊勝。
units.en: He dispatched envoys in such numbers that their carriages stretched in an unbroken line along the road, to investigate Liang and arrest Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.
units.literal: Thus, he sent envoys with coronets and canopies meeting each other on the road, to investigate Liang, arresting Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng.

units.zh: 公孫詭、羊勝匿王後宮。
units.en: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng hid within the king's inner palace.
units.literal: Gongsun Gui and Yang Sheng hid in the king's rear palace.

units.zh: 使者責二千石急，梁相軒丘豹及內史韓安國進諫王，王乃令勝、詭皆自殺，出之。
units.en: The imperial envoys pressed Liang's senior officials relentlessly. The Chancellor of Liang, Xuanqiu Bao, and the Chamberlain Han Anguo went before the king to remonstrate. At last the king ordered Yang Sheng and Gongsun Gui to take their own lives, and their bodies were handed over.
units.literal: The envoys pressed the two thousand shi officials urgently, Liang chancellor Xuanqiu Bao and Chamberlain Han Anguo advanced to remonstrate with the king, the king then ordered Sheng and Gui both to commit suicide, and handed them out.

units.zh: 上由此怨望於梁王。
units.en: From this point on, the emperor bore a lasting resentment toward the King of Liang.
units.literal: The emperor from this resented and distrusted the King of Liang.

units.zh: 梁王恐，乃使韓安國因長公主謝罪太后，然后得釋。
units.en: The King of Liang, now fearful, sent Han Anguo to intercede through the Grand Princess and beg the Empress Dowager's forgiveness. Only then was the matter set aside.
units.literal: The King of Liang feared, so sent Han Anguo through the eldest princess to apologize to the empress dowager, then was released.

units.zh: 上怒稍解，因上書請朝。
units.en: When the emperor's anger had subsided somewhat, the king submitted a memorial requesting permission to attend court.
units.literal: The emperor's anger slightly eased, thus he submitted a memorial requesting to attend court.

units.zh: 既至關，茅蘭說王，使乘布車，從兩騎入，匿於長公主園。
units.en: When they reached the pass, Mao Lan advised the king to ride in a plain cloth-covered cart, enter with only two horsemen as escort, and conceal himself in the Grand Princess's garden.
units.literal: Having reached the pass, Mao Lan advised the king to ride a cloth carriage, enter following two riders, hide in the eldest princess's garden.

units.zh: 漢使使迎王，王已入關，車騎盡居外，不知王處。
units.en: The Han court sent envoys to welcome the king, but he had already slipped through the pass. His chariots and cavalry were all left outside, and no one knew where the king had gone.
units.literal: Han sent envoys to welcome the king, the king had already entered the pass, chariots and cavalry all stayed outside, did not know the king's location.

units.zh: 太后泣曰：「帝殺吾子！」
units.en: The Empress Dowager wept and cried, "The emperor has killed my son!"
units.literal: The empress dowager wept saying: 'The emperor has killed my son!'

units.zh: 景帝憂恐。
units.en: Emperor Jing was deeply alarmed.
units.literal: Emperor Jing was worried and fearful.

units.zh: 於是梁王伏斧質於闕下，謝罪，然後太后、景帝大喜，相泣，復如故。
units.en: The King of Liang then appeared before the palace gate, prostrating himself beside the executioner's axe and block to beg forgiveness for his crimes. The Empress Dowager and Emperor Jing were overjoyed, wept together, and all was restored as before.
units.literal: Thus, the King of Liang prostrated himself with axe and block at the palace gate, apologized for his crimes, then the empress dowager and Emperor Jing greatly rejoiced, wept together, restored as before.

units.zh: 悉召王從官入關。
units.en: All the king's attendants and retinue were then summoned through the pass.
units.literal: He then summoned all of the king's attendants and retinue into the pass.

units.zh: 然景帝益疏王，不同車輦矣。
units.en: Yet from that time on, Emperor Jing grew increasingly distant from the king and no longer shared a carriage with him.
units.literal: Yet Emperor Jing increasingly distanced the king, no longer rode in the same chariot.

units.zh: 三十五年冬，復朝。
units.en: In the winter of his thirty-fifth year, he again traveled to court.
units.literal: In year thirty-five, winter, he attended court again.

units.zh: 上疏欲留，上弗許。
units.en: He petitioned to remain in the capital, but the emperor refused.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial desiring to remain, the emperor did not permit.

units.zh: 歸國，意忽忽不樂。
units.en: He returned to his kingdom in a state of restless melancholy.
units.literal: Returned to his fief, his thoughts were melancholy and unhappy.

units.zh: 北獵良山，有獻牛，足出背上，孝王惡之。
units.en: While hunting in the north at Mount Liang, someone presented him with a monstrous ox whose legs protruded from its back. King Xiao took this as an evil omen.
units.literal: He hunted north at Liangshan, someone presented a cow whose feet came out its back, Prince Xiao considered it ominous.

units.zh: 六月中，病熱，六日卒，謚曰孝王。
units.en: In the middle of the sixth month, he fell ill with a fever and died after six days. He was posthumously titled King Xiao.
units.literal: In the sixth month, he fell ill with fever, died after six days, posthumous title Prince Xiao.

units.zh: 孝王慈孝，每聞太后病，口不能食，居不安寢，常欲留長安侍太后。
units.en: King Xiao was devoted and filial. Whenever he heard that the Empress Dowager was ill, he could not eat and could not sleep, always wishing to remain in Chang'an to attend her in person.
units.literal: Prince Xiao was filial and kind, whenever he heard the empress dowager was ill, could not eat, lived and slept restlessly, constantly wished to remain in Chang'an serving the empress dowager.

units.zh: 太后亦愛之。
units.en: The Empress Dowager loved him dearly in return.
units.literal: The empress dowager also loved him.

units.zh: 及聞梁王薨，竇太后哭極哀，不食，曰：「帝果殺吾子！」
units.en: When she learned that the King of Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou wept inconsolably, refused to eat, and cried, "The emperor has truly killed my son!"
units.literal: When she heard the King of Liang had died, Empress Dowager Dou cried extremely mournfully, did not eat, said: 'The emperor indeed killed my son!'

units.zh: 景帝哀懼，不知所為。
units.en: Emperor Jing was stricken with grief and fear, at a loss for what to do.
units.literal: Emperor Jing was sorrowful and fearful, did not know what to do.

units.zh: 與長公主計之，乃分梁為五國，盡立孝王男五人為王，女五人皆食湯沐邑。
units.en: He consulted with the Grand Princess, and together they divided Liang into five kingdoms, enfeoffing all five of King Xiao's sons as kings. His five daughters were each granted revenue from a bathing fief.
units.literal: Consulted with the eldest princess, then divided Liang into five kingdoms, all enfeoffing Prince Xiao's five sons as kings, five daughters all received bath and grooming fiefs.

units.zh: 於是奏之太后，太后乃說，為帝加壹湌 。
units.en: When this plan was reported to the Empress Dowager, she was pleased and took an extra meal for the emperor's sake.
units.literal: Thus, memorialized to the empress dowager, the empress dowager then was pleased, added one extra meal for the emperor.

units.zh: 梁孝王長子買為梁王，是為共王；
units.en: King Xiao's eldest son, Mai, became King of Liang — he was King Gong.
units.literal: Prince Xiao's eldest son Mai became King of Liang, this was King Gong;

units.zh: 子明為濟川王；
units.en: His son Ming became King of Jichuan.
units.literal: son Ming became King of Jichuan;

units.zh: 子彭離為濟東王；
units.en: His son Pengli became King of Jidong.
units.literal: son Pengli became King of Jidong;

units.zh: 子定為山陽王；
units.en: His son Ding became King of Shanyang.
units.literal: son Ding became King of Shanyang;

units.zh: 子不識為濟陰王。
units.en: And his son Bushi became King of Jiyin.
units.literal: son Bushi became King of Jiyin.

units.zh: 孝王未死時，財以巨萬計，不可勝數。
units.en: Before King Xiao died, his wealth was reckoned in the tens of millions, too vast to count.
units.literal: Before Prince Xiao died, his wealth was counted in millions, beyond numbering.

units.zh: 及死，藏府餘黃金尚四十餘萬斤，他財物稱是。
units.en: At his death, the treasury still held more than four hundred thousand catties of gold, and his other possessions were proportionate.
units.literal: When he died, the treasury still had over 400,000 jin of yellow gold remaining, other valuables matched this.

units.zh: 梁共王三年，景帝崩。
units.en: In the third year of King Gong of Liang, Emperor Jing passed away.
units.literal: In Liang King Gong's third year, Emperor Jing passed away.

units.zh: 共王立七年卒，子襄立，是為平王。
units.en: King Gong reigned for seven years before dying. His son Xiang succeeded him and became King Ping.
units.literal: King Gong reigned seven years and died, his son Xiang succeeded him, becoming King Ping.

units.zh: 梁平王襄十四年，母曰陳太后。
units.en: In the fourteenth year of King Ping of Liang, Xiang — his mother was known as Empress Dowager Chen.
units.literal: Liang King Ping Xiang's fourteenth year, his mother was called Empress Dowager Chen.

units.zh: 共王母曰李太后。
units.en: King Gong's mother was known as Empress Dowager Li.
units.literal: King Gong's mother was called Empress Dowager Li.

units.zh: 李太后，親平王之大母也。
units.en: Empress Dowager Li was in fact King Ping's grandmother.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Li was King Ping's paternal grandmother.

units.zh: 而平王之后姓任，曰任王后。
units.en: King Ping's queen bore the surname Ren and was known as Queen Ren.
units.literal: And King Ping's queen was surnamed Ren, called Queen Ren.

units.zh: 任王后甚有寵於平王襄。
units.en: Queen Ren was greatly favored by King Ping.
units.literal: Queen Ren was greatly favored by King Ping Xiang.

units.zh: 初，孝王在時，有罍樽，直千金。
units.en: In earlier times, when King Xiao was still alive, the house possessed a ceremonial wine vessel worth a thousand catties of gold.
units.literal: Initially, when Prince Xiao was alive, there was a lei zun vessel, worth a thousand jin.

units.zh: 孝王誡後世，善保罍樽，無得以與人。
units.en: King Xiao had left strict instructions to his descendants to guard this vessel well and never give it away.
units.literal: Prince Xiao admonished later generations to carefully preserve the lei zun, not to give it to anyone.

units.zh: 任王后聞而欲得罍樽。
units.en: Queen Ren heard of it and coveted the vessel.
units.literal: Queen Ren heard and desired to obtain the lei zun.

units.zh: 平王大母李太后曰：「先王有命，無得以罍樽與人。
units.en: King Ping's grandmother, Empress Dowager Li, declared, "The former king left explicit orders that the vessel must not be given to anyone.
units.literal: King Ping's paternal grandmother Empress Dowager Li said: 'The former king had commands, not to give the lei zun to anyone.

units.zh: 他物雖百巨萬，猶自恣也。」
units.en: As for other treasures, even those worth a hundred million, you may dispose of them as you please."
units.literal: Other things though a hundred million, still at your own discretion.'

units.zh: 任王后絕欲得之。
units.en: But Queen Ren was determined to have it.
units.literal: Queen Ren absolutely desired to obtain it.

units.zh: 平王襄直使人開府取罍樽，賜任王后。
units.en: King Ping simply ordered his men to open the treasury, remove the vessel, and present it to Queen Ren.
units.literal: King Ping Xiang directly sent men to open the treasury and take the lei zun, granting it to Queen Ren.

units.zh: 李太后大怒，漢使者來，欲自言，平王襄及任王后遮止，閉門，李太后與爭門，措指，遂不得見漢使者。
units.en: Empress Dowager Li was furious. When the Han envoys arrived, she wished to speak with them herself, but King Ping and Queen Ren barred her way and shut the gates. The Empress Dowager struggled at the doors and had her finger caught and crushed in them, and in the end was prevented from seeing the Han envoys.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Li greatly angered, Han envoys came, wished to speak herself, King Ping Xiang and Queen Ren blocked and stopped her, closed the gate, Empress Dowager Li contended at the gate, her finger was pinched, thus could not see the Han envoys.

units.zh: 李太后亦私與食官長及郎中尹霸等士通亂，而王與任王后以此使人風止李太后，李太后內有淫行，亦已。
units.en: Empress Dowager Li had also been carrying on illicit affairs with the Chief of the Food Office and the Gentleman-in-Attendance Yin Ba, among others. The king and Queen Ren used this knowledge to send people to silence her, and since the Empress Dowager was compromised by her own misconduct, the matter was dropped.
units.literal: Empress Dowager Li also privately had illicit relations with the food official chief and Gentleman-in-Attendance Yin Ba and other scholars, while the king and Queen Ren used this to send people to warn and stop Empress Dowager Li, Empress Dowager Li internally had lewd conduct, and that was all.

units.zh: 後病薨。
units.en: Later she fell ill and died.
units.literal: Later she fell ill and died.

units.zh: 病時，任后未嘗請病；
units.en: During her illness, Queen Ren never once inquired after her health.
units.literal: When ill, Queen Ren never inquired about the illness;

units.zh: 薨，又不持喪。
units.en: When she died, the queen did not observe the mourning rites.
units.literal: When she died, moreover did not observe mourning.

units.zh: 元朔中，睢陽人類犴反者，人有辱其父，而與淮陽太守客出同車。
units.en: During the Yuanshuo era, a man from Suiyang named Lei Qianfan nursed a grudge against someone who had insulted his father. This enemy happened to ride out in the same carriage as a guest of the Governor of Huaiyang.
units.literal: In Yuanshuo period, among Suiyang people there was one Lei Qianfan; someone had insulted his father, and that enemy went out in the same carriage as the Huaiyang governor's guest.

units.zh: 太守客出下車，類犴反殺其仇於車上而去。
units.en: When the governor's guest stepped down from the carriage, Lei Qianfan stabbed his enemy to death on the spot and fled.
units.literal: The governor's guest got out and descended from the carriage, Lei Qian stabbed and killed his enemy on the carriage and left.

units.zh: 淮陽太守怒，以讓梁二千石。
units.en: The Governor of Huaiyang was incensed and reprimanded the senior officials of Liang.
units.literal: The Huaiyang governor angered, rebuked Liang's two thousand shi officials.

units.zh: 二千石以下求反甚急，執反親戚。
units.en: The officials of two thousand bushels and below pursued the fugitive relentlessly and arrested his kinsmen.
units.literal: The two thousand shi officials and below sought the rebel very urgently, arrested the rebel's relatives.

units.zh: 反知國陰事，乃上變事，具告知王與大母爭樽狀。
units.en: The fugitive, who knew the kingdom's hidden scandals, reported these irregularities to the authorities, giving a full account of how the king and his grandmother had quarreled over the ceremonial vessel.
units.literal: The rebel knew the state's secret matters, thus reported the irregularity, fully informed of the king and paternal grandmother contending over the zun vessel situation.

units.zh: 時丞相以下見知之，欲以傷梁長吏，其書聞天子。
units.en: The Chancellor and other officials at court saw in this an opportunity to bring charges against Liang's senior administrators, and the report reached the Son of Heaven.
units.literal: At the time the chancellor and below saw and knew it, wished to harm Liang's senior officials, the memorial reached the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 天子下吏驗問，有之。
units.en: The Son of Heaven dispatched officials to investigate, and the charges proved true.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven sent officials to investigate and question, it was true.

units.zh: 公卿請廢襄為庶人。
units.en: The high ministers petitioned to have Xiang deposed and reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: The dukes and ministers requested to depose Xiang as commoner.

units.zh: 天子曰：「李太后有淫行，而梁王襄無良師傅，故陷不義。」
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "Empress Dowager Li was guilty of misconduct, and King Xiang of Liang had no worthy tutors to guide him, so he fell into wrongdoing."
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said: 'Empress Dowager Li had lewd conduct, and Liang King Xiang had no good tutors, thus fell into unrighteousness.'

units.zh: 乃削梁八城，梟任王后首于市。
units.en: He stripped Liang of eight cities and had Queen Ren beheaded, her head displayed in the marketplace.
units.literal: Thus, he cut away eight Liang cities, beheaded Queen Ren in the market.

units.zh: 梁餘尚有十城。
units.en: Liang was left with only ten cities.
units.literal: Liang still had ten cities remaining.

units.zh: 襄立三十九年卒，謚為平王。
units.en: Xiang reigned for thirty-nine years before dying. He was posthumously titled King Ping.
units.literal: Xiang reigned thirty-nine years and died, posthumous title King Ping.

units.zh: 子無傷立為梁王也。
units.en: His son Wushang succeeded him as King of Liang.
units.literal: His son Wushang succeeded as King of Liang.

units.zh: 濟川王明者，梁孝王子，以桓邑侯孝景中六年為濟川王。
units.en: King Ming of Jichuan was a son of King Xiao. Formerly the Marquis of Huanyi, he was made King of Jichuan in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: King Ming of Jichuan was Prince Xiao's son, as Marquis of Huanyi in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jichuan.

units.zh: 七歲，坐射殺其中尉，漢有司請誅，天子弗忍誅，廢明為庶人。
units.en: After seven years, he was convicted of shooting and killing his Commandant of the Capital. The Han officials petitioned for his execution, but the Son of Heaven could not bring himself to carry it out and instead deposed Ming to the status of a commoner.
units.literal: Seven years, because he shot and killed his commandery lieutenant, Han officials requested execution, the Son of Heaven could not bear to execute, deposed Ming as commoner.

units.zh: 遷房陵，地入于漢為郡。
units.en: He was exiled to Fangling, and his territory was absorbed into the Han empire as a commandery.
units.literal: Relocated to Fangling, the land entered Han as a commandery.

units.zh: 濟東王彭離者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為濟東王。
units.en: King Pengli of Jidong was a son of King Xiao who was made King of Jidong in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: King Pengli of Jidong was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jidong.

units.zh: 二十九年，彭離驕悍，無人君禮，昏暮私與其奴、亡命少年數十人行剽殺人，取財物以為好。
units.en: Over twenty-nine years, Pengli grew arrogant and savage, heedless of the deportment expected of a ruler. Under cover of darkness, he would steal out with his slaves and bands of fugitive youths, dozens strong, to rob and murder travelers, taking their goods for his amusement.
units.literal: Twenty-nine years, Pengli was arrogant and fierce, without ruler's ritual, at dusk privately went with his slaves and fugitive youths several dozen people to plunder and kill people, taking wealth as pleasure.

units.zh: 所殺發覺者百餘人，國皆知之，莫敢夜行。
units.en: More than a hundred murders were eventually discovered. Everyone in the kingdom knew of his crimes, and no one dared travel after dark.
units.literal: Those killed and discovered were over a hundred people, the kingdom all knew it, none dared travel at night.

units.zh: 所殺者子上書言。
units.en: The son of one of his victims submitted a memorial denouncing him.
units.literal: The son of one who was killed submitted a memorial to report.

units.zh: 漢有司請誅，上不忍，廢以為庶人，遷上庸，地入于漢，為大河郡。
units.en: The Han officials again petitioned for execution, but the emperor could not bring himself to agree. Pengli was deposed to commoner status and exiled to Shangyong. His territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Dahe.
units.literal: Han officials requested execution, the emperor could not bear it, deposed as commoner, relocated to Shangyong, land entered Han, became Dahe commandery.

units.zh: 山陽哀王定者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為山陽王。
units.en: King Ai of Shanyang, whose name was Ding, was a son of King Xiao. He was made King of Shanyang in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: King Ai Ding of Shanyang was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Shanyang.

units.zh: 九年卒，無子，國除，地入于漢，為山陽郡。
units.en: He died after nine years on the throne, leaving no heir. The kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Shanyang.
units.literal: Nine years died, no son, kingdom abolished, land entered Han, became Shanyang commandery.

units.zh: 濟陰哀王不識者，梁孝王子，以孝景中六年為濟陰王。
units.en: King Ai of Jiyin, whose name was Bushi, was a son of King Xiao. He was made King of Jiyin in the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: King Ai Bushi of Jiyin was Prince Xiao's son, in Xiaojing middle year 6 became King of Jiyin.

units.zh: 一歲卒，無子，國除，地入于漢，為濟陰郡。
units.en: He died after only one year, leaving no heir. The kingdom was abolished, and its territory was absorbed into the Han empire as the Commandery of Jiyin.
units.literal: One year died, no son, kingdom abolished, land entered Han, became Jiyin commandery.

units.zh: 太史公曰：梁孝王雖以親愛之故，王膏腴之地，然會漢家隆盛，百姓殷富，故能植其財貨，廣宮室，車服擬於天子。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: King Xiao of Liang was granted fertile lands because of the close affection he enjoyed. Yet he was able to amass such wealth, expand his palaces, and adopt carriages and robes rivaling those of the Son of Heaven only because his reign coincided with the flourishing of the Han dynasty. At that time, the common people were prosperous and well-off.
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Though Prince Xiao of Liang because of close affection was enfeoffed with fertile lands, yet meeting when the Han house was flourishing, people wealthy, thus could accumulate his wealth, expand palaces, carriages and robes comparable to the Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 然亦僭矣。
units.en: Even so, this was presumptuous indeed.
units.literal: Yet it was also presumptuous.

units.zh: 褚先生曰：臣為郎時，聞之於宮殿中老郎吏好事者稱道之也。
units.en: Master Chu says: When I served as a Gentleman at court, I heard this tale from old officials in the palace halls who were fond of recounting such stories.
units.literal: Master Chu says: When your servant was a gentleman, heard it from old gentleman officials in the palace halls who liked history relating it.

units.zh: 竊以為令梁孝王怨望，欲為不善者，事從中生。
units.en: I believe that the resentment that drove King Xiao of Liang to contemplate wrongdoing arose from within the court itself.
units.literal: I privately consider that causing Prince Xiao of Liang to resent and wish to do evil, the matter arose from within.

units.zh: 今太后，女主也，以愛少子故，欲令梁王為太子。
units.en: The Empress Dowager, a woman wielding power, wished out of love for her youngest son to make the King of Liang the crown prince.
units.literal: Now the empress dowager is a female ruler, because she loved the youngest son, wished to make the King of Liang crown prince.

units.zh: 大臣不時正言其不可狀，阿意治小，私說意以受賞賜，非忠臣也。
units.en: The great ministers failed to speak up forthrightly against this impropriety at the proper time. Instead, they flattered and dealt in trivialities, whispering agreeable words in hopes of rewards — the behavior not of loyal ministers.
units.literal: Ministers did not timely correctly speak of the impropriety, flattered and handled trifles, privately spoke pleasing words to receive rewards and grants, not loyal ministers.

units.zh: 齊如魏其侯竇嬰之正言也，何以有後禍？
units.en: Had they all spoken as forthrightly as the Marquis of Weiqi, Dou Ying, what later calamity could have arisen?
units.literal: How like Marquis Weiqi Dou Ying's correct speech—what future calamity would there be?

units.zh: 景帝與王燕見，侍太后飲，景帝曰：「千秋萬歲之後傳王。」
units.en: Emperor Jing and the king attended a banquet together, serving the Empress Dowager wine. Emperor Jing said, "When I am gone, I shall pass the throne to you."
units.literal: Emperor Jing and the king attended a banquet, serving the Empress Dowager wine. Emperor Jing said, "After a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, I shall pass the throne to you."

units.zh: 太后喜說。
units.en: The Empress Dowager was overjoyed.
units.literal: The empress dowager was pleased and happy.

units.zh: 竇嬰在前，據地言曰：「漢法之約，傳子適孫，今帝何以得傳弟，擅亂高帝約乎！」
units.en: But Dou Ying stepped forward, struck the ground, and declared, "The covenant of Han law mandates succession from father to son and grandson. How can the emperor pass the throne to his brother and recklessly violate the compact established by Emperor Gaozu!"
units.literal: Dou Ying was in front, struck the ground and said: 'The Han law's covenant is to pass to son and grandson, now how can the emperor pass to younger brother, arbitrarily disrupt Gaozu's covenant!'

units.zh: 於是景帝默然無聲。
units.en: Emperor Jing fell silent.
units.literal: Thus, Emperor Jing was silent without sound.

units.zh: 太后意不說。
units.en: The Empress Dowager was displeased.
units.literal: The empress dowager's intent was displeased.

units.zh: 故成王與小弱弟立樹下，取一桐葉以與之，曰：「吾用封汝。」
units.en: In ancient times, King Cheng of Zhou stood with his young brother beneath a tree, plucked a paulownia leaf, and said, "With this I shall enfeoff you."
units.literal: Thus, King Cheng stood with his young weak brother under a tree, took one paulownia leaf and gave it to him, saying: 'I will use this to enfeoff you.'

units.zh: 周公聞之，進見曰：「天王封弟，甚善。」
units.en: When the Duke of Zhou heard of this, he came forward and said, "The Son of Heaven has enfeoffed his younger brother — this is most excellent."
units.literal: When the Duke of Zhou heard of it, he came forward and said, "The Son of Heaven has enfeoffed his younger brother — this is excellent."

units.zh: 成王曰：「吾直與戲耳。」
units.en: King Cheng replied, "I was only playing."
units.literal: King Cheng said: 'I was just playing with him.'

units.zh: 周公曰：「人主無過舉，不當有戲言，言之必行之。」
units.en: The Duke of Zhou said, "A ruler must make no careless gesture and speak no idle word. What the ruler says, he must carry out."
units.literal: The Duke of Zhou said: 'A ruler has no erroneous actions, should not have joking words—words spoken must be carried out.'

units.zh: 於是乃封小弟以應縣。
units.en: And so the young brother was indeed enfeoffed with the district of Ying.
units.literal: Thus, he enfeoffed the young brother with Ying county.

units.zh: 是後成王沒齒不敢有戲言，言必行之。
units.en: From that day forward, King Cheng never dared to speak in jest for the rest of his life; every word he uttered, he carried out.
units.literal: After this King Cheng to the end of his life dared not have joking words, words spoken must be carried out.

units.zh: 《孝經》曰：「非法不言，非道不行。」
units.en: The Classic of Filial Piety says, "Speak nothing that is contrary to propriety; do nothing that is contrary to the Way."
units.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Do not speak what is not according to law, do not act what is not according to the Way.'

units.zh: 此聖人之法言也。
units.en: These are the guiding words of the sages.
units.literal: This is the legal words of the sages.

units.zh: 今主上不宜出好言於梁王。
units.en: The sovereign should never have spoken such encouraging words to the King of Liang.
units.literal: Now the sovereign should not speak favorable words to the King of Liang.

units.zh: 梁王上有太后之重，驕蹇日久，數聞景帝好言，千秋萬世之後傳王，而實不行。
units.en: The King of Liang, backed by the Empress Dowager's formidable influence, had long grown arrogant and willful. He had repeatedly heard Emperor Jing's promise that the throne would pass to him after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years, yet this promise was never fulfilled.
units.literal: The King of Liang above has the empress dowager's weight, arrogant and willful for a long time, repeatedly heard Emperor Jing's favorable words that after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years he would pass to the king, yet in reality not carried out.

units.zh: 又諸侯王朝見天子，漢法凡當四見耳。
units.en: Furthermore, when feudal kings attend court before the Son of Heaven, Han law prescribes only four audiences in all.
units.literal: Moreover, feudal lords' kings attending court to see the Son of Heaven, Han law generally should be four audiences.

units.zh: 始到，入小見；
units.en: Upon first arriving, there is an informal audience.
units.literal: First arrival, enter for small audience;

units.zh: 到正月朔旦，奉皮薦璧玉賀正月，法見；
units.en: On New Year's Day, the king presents leather, recommends jade discs, and offers congratulations at a formal audience.
units.literal: Arrive at New Year's first dawn, present leather and recommend jade discs to congratulate New Year, formal audience;

units.zh: 後三日，為王置酒，賜金錢財物；
units.en: Three days later, a banquet is held in the king's honor, and he is presented with gifts of gold, money, and valuables.
units.literal: Three days later, set wine for the king, grant gold money and valuables;

units.zh: 後二日，復入小見，辭去。
units.en: Two days after that, there is a final informal audience, after which the king takes his leave and departs.
units.literal: Two days later, again enter for small audience, take leave and depart.

units.zh: 凡留長安不過二十日。
units.en: In total, the stay in Chang'an should not exceed twenty days.
units.literal: Altogether remaining in Chang'an not over twenty days.

units.zh: 小見者，燕見於禁門內，飲於省中，非士人所得入也。
units.en: The informal audience is a private meeting within the palace gates, with drinking in the inner chambers — a privilege not extended to ordinary scholars.
units.literal: Small audience means banquet meeting within the forbidden gates, drinking in the administration quarters, not where scholars can enter.

units.zh: 今梁王西朝，因留，且半歲。
units.en: Yet the King of Liang came west to court and stayed on for nearly half a year.
units.literal: Now the King of Liang comes west to court, thus stays, nearly half a year.

units.zh: 入與人主同輦，出與同車。
units.en: At court, he rode in the same carriage as the emperor, and abroad he shared the emperor's chariot.
units.literal: When entering court he rode in the same carriage as the ruler; when going abroad he rode in the same chariot.

units.zh: 示風以大言而實不與，令出怨言，謀畔逆，乃隨而憂之，不亦遠乎！
units.en: To make grand promises in word while refusing to deliver in deed, thereby provoking resentment and scheming, and then to follow up with anxiety over the consequences — is this not the height of shortsightedness!
units.literal: To hold out great promises in word yet in deed not deliver, thereby provoking resentment and plotting rebellion and treason, and then afterward to fret over it — is this not utterly perverse!

units.zh: 非大賢人，不知退讓。
units.en: Only a person of the highest virtue knows when to yield and step back.
units.literal: If not a great worthy person, does not know yielding and retreating.

units.zh: 今漢之儀法，朝見賀正月者，常一王與四侯俱朝見，十餘歲一至。
units.en: Under Han ritual protocol, those attending the New Year court audience are normally one king and four marquises at a time, and each comes only once every ten or more years.
units.literal: Now Han's ritual law, those attending court and congratulating New Year, normally one king with four marquises together attend court, once every ten or more years.

units.zh: 今梁王常比年入朝見，久留。
units.en: Yet the King of Liang attended court year after year and stayed for prolonged periods.
units.literal: Now the King of Liang constantly attends court consecutively, stays long.

units.zh: 鄙語曰「驕子不孝」，非惡言也。
units.en: The common saying goes, "A spoiled son is an unfilial son" — and this is no idle proverb.
units.literal: The vulgar saying goes 'spoiled son is unfilial', not evil words.

units.zh: 故諸侯王當為置良師傅，相忠言之士，如汲黯、韓長孺等，敢直言極諫，安得有患害！
units.en: This is why feudal kings should be given worthy tutors and chancellors, men of loyal counsel such as Ji An and Han Changru, who dare to speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve. If this were done, how could any calamity arise!
units.literal: Therefore, feudal kings should be given good tutors and chancellors, loyal speaking officials, like Ji An, Han Changru and such, who dare to speak directly and remonstrate extremely—how can there be calamity and harm!

units.zh: 蓋聞梁王西入朝，謁竇太后，燕見，與景帝俱侍坐於太后前，語言私說。
units.en: I have heard that the King of Liang traveled west to court, paid his respects to Empress Dowager Dou, and was granted a private audience. He sat together with Emperor Jing before the Empress Dowager, and they spoke freely among themselves.
units.literal: I heard that the King of Liang entered west to court, greeted Empress Dowager Dou, banquet meeting, together with Emperor Jing served and sat before the empress dowager, private language pleased.

units.zh: 太后謂帝曰：「吾聞殷道親親，周道尊尊，其義一也。
units.en: The Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "I have heard that the way of the Yin dynasty was to cherish kinship, while the way of the Zhou was to honor authority, and in principle these amount to the same thing.
units.literal: The empress dowager told the emperor: 'I heard Yin way loves relatives, Zhou way honors superiors, their meanings are one.

units.zh: 安車大駕，用梁孝王為寄。」
units.en: When the great carriage and imperial procession pass to another, let King Xiao of Liang be the one entrusted with them."
units.literal: Peaceful carriage great procession, use Prince Xiao of Liang as the heir.'

units.zh: 景帝跪席舉身曰：「諾。」
units.en: Emperor Jing straightened on his mat, bowed, and said, "Yes."
units.literal: Emperor Jing knelt on the mat and raised his body saying: 'Yes.'

units.zh: 罷酒出，帝召袁盎諸大臣通經術者曰：「太后言如是，何謂也？」
units.en: After the banquet ended, they withdrew. The emperor then summoned Yuan Ang and other ministers learned in the classics and asked, "The Empress Dowager speaks thus. What does she mean?"
units.literal: Finished the wine and went out, the emperor summoned Yuan Ang and various ministers versed in classics saying: 'The empress dowager speaks like this, what does it mean?'

units.zh: 皆對曰：「太后意欲立梁王為帝太子。」
units.en: They all replied, "The Empress Dowager intends to establish the King of Liang as the imperial heir."
units.literal: All replied: 'The empress dowager intends to establish the King of Liang as imperial crown prince.'

units.zh: 帝問其狀，袁盎等曰：「殷道親親者，立弟。
units.en: The emperor asked them to explain. Yuan Ang and the others said, "The way of the Yin dynasty was to cherish kinship, and so the younger brother was made heir.
units.literal: The emperor asked the circumstances, Yuan Ang and others said: 'Yin way loves relatives establishes younger brother.

units.zh: 周道尊尊者，立子。
units.en: The way of the Zhou was to honor seniority, and so the son was made heir.
units.literal: Zhou way honors superiors establishes son.

units.zh: 殷道質，質者法天，親其所親，故立弟。
units.en: The way of Yin valued substance. Substance follows Heaven, which draws close those who are nearest, and so the younger brother was made heir.
units.literal: Yin way substantial, substantial follows Heaven, loves those close to it, thus establishes younger brother.

units.zh: 周道文，文者法地，尊者敬也，敬其本始，故立長子。
units.en: The way of Zhou valued refinement. Refinement follows Earth, which honors authority — and to honor authority is to respect one's origins, so the eldest son was made heir.
units.literal: Zhou way cultured, cultured follows Earth, honor means respect, respects its origin, thus establishes eldest son.

units.zh: 周道，太子死，立適孫。
units.en: Under the Zhou system, if the crown prince dies, the legitimate grandson succeeds.
units.literal: Zhou way, crown prince dies, establishes proper grandson.

units.zh: 殷道。
units.en: Under the Yin system —
units.literal: Yin way.

units.zh: 太子死，立其弟。」
units.en: if the crown prince dies, his younger brother succeeds."
units.literal: Crown prince dies, establishes his younger brother.'

units.zh: 帝曰：「於公何如？」
units.en: The emperor asked, "What is your view, gentlemen?"
units.literal: The emperor said: 'To you gentlemen what is it?'

units.zh: 皆對曰：「方今漢家法周，周道不得立弟，當立子。
units.en: They all replied, "The Han house now follows the Zhou system. Under the way of Zhou, a younger brother cannot be made heir; the son must succeed.
units.literal: All replied: 'Now the Han house follows Zhou, Zhou way cannot establish younger brother, should establish son.

units.zh: 故春秋所以非宋宣公。
units.en: This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals censures Duke Xuan of Song.
units.literal: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals criticizes Duke Xuan of Song.

units.zh: 宋宣公死，不立子而與弟。
units.en: When Duke Xuan of Song died, he did not establish his son but passed the throne to his younger brother.
units.literal: Duke Xuan of Song died, did not establish son but gave to younger brother.

units.zh: 弟受國死，復反之與兄之子。
units.en: When the younger brother received the state and later died, he returned it to his elder brother's son.
units.literal: Younger brother received the state died, again returned it to elder brother's son.

units.zh: 弟之子爭之，以為我當代父後，即刺殺兄子。
units.en: But the younger brother's son disputed this, reasoning that he should succeed his own father, and so he assassinated the elder brother's son.
units.literal: Younger brother's son contended for it, considering I should succeed father's place, thus stabbed and killed elder brother's son.

units.zh: 以故國亂，禍不絕。
units.en: As a result, the state was thrown into chaos and calamities followed without end.
units.literal: Therefore, the state was chaotic, calamities did not cease.

units.zh: 故春秋曰『君子大居正，宋之禍宣公為之』。
units.en: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals declares, 'The gentleman holds fast to what is correct; the calamity that befell Song was brought about by Duke Xuan.'
units.literal: Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals says 'The gentleman greatly occupies correctness, Song's calamity Duke Xuan made it.'

units.zh: 臣請見太后白之。」
units.en: We request permission to see the Empress Dowager and explain this to her."
units.literal: Your servants request to see the empress dowager and inform her.'

units.zh: 袁盎等入見太后：「太后言欲立梁王，梁王即終，欲誰立？」
units.en: Yuan Ang and the others entered and asked the Empress Dowager, "If Your Majesty establishes the King of Liang, and the King of Liang later dies, whom would you choose after him?"
units.literal: Yuan Ang and the others went in to see the Empress Dowager and asked, "Your Majesty wishes to establish the King of Liang as heir. But if the King of Liang should die, whom would you then wish to establish?"

units.zh: 太后曰：「吾復立帝子。」
units.en: The Empress Dowager said, "Then I would establish the emperor's son."
units.literal: The empress dowager said: 'I will again establish the emperor's son.'

units.zh: 袁盎等以宋宣公不立正，生禍，禍亂後五世不絕，小不忍害大義狀報太后。
units.en: Yuan Ang and the others presented the case of Duke Xuan of Song, who had failed to follow the proper line of succession and thereby brought about a calamity that plagued his state for five generations. They explained to the Empress Dowager how a small indulgence could undermine the greater good.
units.literal: Yuan Ang and others with Duke Xuan of Song not establishing properly, produced calamity, calamity and chaos after five generations not ceased, little intolerance harming great righteousness, reported to the empress dowager.

units.zh: 太后乃解說，即使梁王歸就國。
units.en: The Empress Dowager was persuaded and abandoned the idea, immediately directing the King of Liang to return to his kingdom.
units.literal: The empress dowager then dispelled her idea, immediately had the King of Liang return to his fief.

units.zh: 而梁王聞其義出於袁盎諸大臣所，怨望，使人來殺袁盎。
units.en: When the King of Liang learned that the arguments against him had come from Yuan Ang and the other ministers, he was consumed with resentment and sent men to assassinate Yuan Ang.
units.literal: And the King of Liang heard that the righteousness came from Yuan Ang and the various ministers, resented, sent men to come kill Yuan Ang.

units.zh: 袁盎顧之曰：「我所謂袁將軍者也，公得毋誤乎？」
units.en: Yuan Ang turned to face the assassin and said, "I am the one known as General Yuan. Are you sure you have the right man?"
units.literal: Yuan Ang looked at him saying: 'The one called General Yuan is me, sir has not mistaken?'

units.zh: 刺者曰：「是矣！」
units.en: The assassin replied, "You are the one!"
units.literal: The assassin said: 'Correct!'

units.zh: 刺之，置其劍，劍著身。
units.en: He stabbed him and left the sword behind, still lodged in the body.
units.literal: Stabbed him, left his sword, the sword stuck in the body.

units.zh: 視其劍，新治。
units.en: When they examined the sword, they found it was newly forged.
units.literal: Looked at his sword, newly forged.

units.zh: 問長安中削厲工，工曰：「梁郎某子來治此劍。」
units.en: They inquired among the sword-smiths of Chang'an, and one of them said, "A young attendant from Liang came to have this sword made."
units.literal: Asked Chang'an's sword sharpening workers, the worker said: 'A Liang attendant some son came to forge this sword.'

units.zh: 以此知而發覺之，發使者捕逐之。
units.en: This led to the discovery of the plot, and envoys were dispatched to apprehend and pursue the culprits.
units.literal: With this knew and discovered it, sent envoys to capture and pursue them.

units.zh: 獨梁王所欲殺大臣十餘人，文吏窮本之，謀反端頗見。
units.en: In all, the King of Liang had targeted more than ten ministers for assassination. When the legal officials traced the matter to its source, clear signs of a conspiracy to rebel emerged.
units.literal: Only the King of Liang desired to kill ministers more than ten, the civil officials investigated to the root, rebellion signs much appeared.

units.zh: 太后不食，日夜泣不止。
units.en: The Empress Dowager refused to eat and wept day and night without ceasing.
units.literal: The empress dowager did not eat, day and night wept without stopping.

units.zh: 景帝甚憂之，問公卿大臣，大臣以為遣經術吏往治之，乃可解。
units.en: Emperor Jing was deeply troubled and consulted his ministers. They advised that officials well-versed in the classics be sent to handle the matter, as this was the only way to resolve the crisis.
units.literal: Emperor Jing greatly worried about it, asked the dukes and ministers, ministers considered sending classic versed officials to handle it, then could resolve.

units.zh: 於是遣田叔、呂季主往治之。
units.en: Accordingly, Tian Shu and Lu Jizhu were dispatched to handle the matter.
units.literal: Thus, sent Tian Shu, Lu Jizhu to handle it.

units.zh: 此二人皆通經術，知大禮。
units.en: Both men were thoroughly versed in the classics and understood the demands of high propriety.
units.literal: These two both versed in classics, knew great ritual.

units.zh: 來還，至霸昌廄，取火悉燒梁之反辭，但空手來對景帝。
units.en: On their return journey, when they reached the Bachang post station, they set fire to all the incriminating documents from Liang and came before Emperor Jing with empty hands.
units.literal: Coming back, arrived at Bachang stable, took fire and completely burned Liang's rebellion documents, but came with empty hands to answer Emperor Jing.

units.zh: 景帝曰：「何如？」
units.en: Emperor Jing asked, "What did you find?"
units.literal: Emperor Jing said: 'What is it like?'

units.zh: 對曰：「言梁王不知也。
units.en: They replied, "The King of Liang knew nothing of the plot.
units.literal: They replied, "We report that the King of Liang knew nothing of it.

units.zh: 造為之者，獨其幸臣羊勝、公孫詭之屬為之耳。
units.en: The conspirators were solely his favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and their associates.
units.literal: Those who fabricated it were only his favored ministers Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui and such did it.

units.zh: 謹以伏誅死，梁王無恙也。」
units.en: They have already submitted to the law and been put to death. The King of Liang is well and bears no guilt."
units.literal: They have already submitted to execution and been put to death. The King of Liang is unharmed."

units.zh: 景帝喜說，曰：「急趨謁太后。」
units.en: Emperor Jing was delighted and said, "Go at once and report this to the Empress Dowager."
units.literal: Emperor Jing pleased and happy, said: 'Quickly go announce to the empress dowager.'

units.zh: 太后聞之，立起坐湌，氣平復。
units.en: When the Empress Dowager heard the news, she rose at once, took a meal, and her spirits were restored.
units.literal: The empress dowager heard it, immediately rose and sat drinking, her energy calmed and recovered.

units.zh: 故曰，不通經術知古今之大禮，不可以為三公及左右近臣。
units.en: Therefore, it is said: those who are not versed in the classics and do not understand the great principles of propriety, both ancient and modern, are unfit to serve as one of the Three Excellencies or as a minister close to the throne.
units.literal: Therefore, it is said, if not versed in classics and knowing ancient and modern great ritual, cannot serve as three dukes and left and right close ministers.

units.zh: 少見之人，如從管中闚天也。
units.en: Those of narrow vision are like men trying to see the sky through a tube.
units.literal: People of little knowledge are like peeking at heaven from a tube.
